summary: Full e2e validation of Super Admin per-company limit overrides, plan editing, and orphan-member repair. Backend: 6/6 pytest tests pass (members merged list w/ has_membership, idempotent create_membership_from_user, set+clear limit_overrides reflected in GET /organizations/{id}, GET /plans returns starter/professional/enterprise, PUT /plans/{id} updates only limits while preserving name/price, check_usage_limit honors company override over plan default — verified by setting events_per_month=2 on the demo company and getting allowed=false, limit=2 from /api/org/usage/check/events_created). Frontend (Playwright on real preview URL, logged in as margaret super-admin): (1) /super-admin/organizations/company_02c27f41dc78 -> Overview tab -> LimitOverridesCard visible; typed 100 into events_per_month, clicked Guardar, saw 'Límites actualizados' toast, reloaded -> value persists at 100; clicked 'Limpiar todo' -> all inputs cleared and 'Usando plan (30)' label re-appears. (2) Members tab renders cleanly — the previously orphan user is now shown with role=admin and a normal membership row (it was auto-repaired by the backend idempotency test moments earlier, so no 'Sin membresía' badge remained at the time of the UI test; the create flow is verified via backend). (3) /super-admin/settings -> Planes tab renders 3 plan cards (plans-editor + plan-card-{id} testids present); changed plan_starter events_per_month to 75, saved -> 'Plan actualizado' toast -> reloaded the page and re-opened the Planes tab -> value persisted at 75 -> reverted to 50 successfully. No console errors, no overlay issues, no broken integrations.
critical_code_review_comments: update_org_limit_overrides currently silently ignores unknown keys (continue). Consider returning 400 for typos so the admin notices their input was dropped.

update_plan_admin returns {success:true, changed:false} when only the updated_at would change, but it ALWAYS overwrites updated_at via patch in the changed=true branch — minor inconsistency, not blocking. The unchanged branch correctly avoids the write.
get_org_members loops users.find_one inside the memberships loop (N+1). For orgs with hundreds of memberships this could be slow. Consider $in batch lookup. Not critical at preview scale.
check_usage_limit casts the override via int(...) and silently falls back to plan limit on TypeError/ValueError. Logging a warning when an admin-stored override is malformed would help debugging.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend test file at /app/backend/tests/test_super_admin_limit_overrides_plans.py is fully idempotent — it resolves demo company_id by logging in as demo.agency (NOT by name match, which was ambiguous across 51 orgs), snapshots existing limit_overrides before mutation and restores them in a finally block, reverts plan_starter limits to defaults.
